selected_records.title: Unmanned warfare has now expanded to the high seas. Is the U.S. ready?

article.body:
High-seas unmanned warfare: U.S. Navy contracts with General Atomics for Sea Hunter UUVs

The U.S. Navy has contracted General Atomics for the purchase of 16 Sea Hunter unmanned underwater vehicles (UUVs), marking an expansion of unmanned warfare to the high seas. The contract, valued at $43 million, will provide the Navy with advanced underwater capabilities for surveillance, reconnaissance, and mine countermeasures. This commercial relationship change targets naval operations and competitively positions General Atomics as a key supplier of unmanned underwater technology to the U.S. military. The number that matters is the contract value of $43 million.

maren_repair.original_article:
High-seas unmanned warfare: no transaction established

The assigned report describes unmanned warfare expanding to the high seas, but the available evidence identifies no buyer, recipient, contract or amount. It establishes no change in a commercial relationship.
